title: Swarmbreak just launched in Early Access
author: forgefire
selftext:
Hey all,



A while back I posted Swarmbreak here, and it's now out in Early Access on Steam. Here's a quick update on what's changed and how a couple of things got made.



What's new since last time:



\- \*\*New animations.\*\* I rebuilt the sprites so each character is a single 3D model, built in a Python script and baked out to pixel art. That gave me 16 facings for the player and 8 for each enemy without drawing every angle by hand (second image).

\- \*\*Perk overhaul.\*\* Ranks, rarities, families and branching perks. Level-ups now deal one card for your current build, one new perk and one wild card.

\- \*\*Threat ladder.\*\* Seven difficulty tiers, where each one changes a rule of the run instead of just adding HP.



On the workflow side: I use Claude Code for most of the programming. Balance and game feel are still where most of my own time goes. The most useful habit has been keeping a [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) with project rules (how pooled objects get reset, no epsilon comparisons in tests, how the demo build is gated) so the same mistakes don't keep coming back.



 Screenshots and trailer clips come from a small "shot studio" tool that sets up a scene and renders it through the game's own renderer, which made the marketing side a lot less painful. This has honestly been amazing when working on marketing, screenshots, trailers etc.



The plan for Early Access is balance first, then more meta progression, and maybe more weapons and enemy types if they turn out to make the game better. I'm expecting somewhere around 3-6 months.



Happy to answer questions about the workflow or the sprite pipeline.



Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4450820/Swarmbreak/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4450820/Swarmbreak/)
